questions.q: What does `ago(24h)` return in a KQL query?
options: The timestamp 24 hours before the moment the query runs
The total number of events in the last 24 hours
A Boolean indicating whether 24 hours have passed since the table was created
The timestamp exactly 24 hours in the future
questions.explain: ago() computes a timestamp that many units before now; used with where TimeGenerated > ago(24h), it narrows a query to the last day.

questions.q: What does `join kind=inner` do when combining two tables?
options: Keeps only rows that have a match on the join column in both tables
Keeps every row from both tables regardless of whether they match
Keeps only rows from the left table, ignoring the right table entirely
Merges the two tables' schemas without comparing any row values
questions.explain: An inner join keeps only rows with a matching value in both tables — here, sign-ins whose IP also appears in the threat intelligence table.

options: The table before the join operator (SigninLogs in this example)
The table inside the join's parentheses (ThreatIntelligenceIndicator)
A reserved keyword with no connection to either table
The column with the alphabetically first name
questions.explain: $left refers to the table piped into join; $right refers to the table named inside the join's parentheses — needed here because the columns have different names.

questions.q: Why does the example query filter the ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table with its own `where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)` before the join happens?
options: Filtering both sides down first keeps the join fast against tables that can have millions of rows
KQL requires every table in a join to have an identical where clause
It has no effect on performance, only on formatting
It prevents the join from running at all if omitted
questions.explain: Narrowing both tables to the relevant time window before joining, rather than joining everything first, is what keeps the query efficient at scale.

questions.q: What does each row represent in the final query `SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | join kind=inner (ThreatIntelligenceIndicator | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)) on $left.IPAddress == $right.NetworkIP | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, ThreatType, Description`?
options: A sign-in in the last 24 hours from an IP address already flagged in threat intelligence, with the reason why
Every sign-in in SigninLogs, regardless of any threat intelligence match
A single aggregate count of all flagged sign-ins
A list of all known threat intelligence indicators, with no connection to sign-in activity
questions.explain: The inner join only keeps sign-ins whose IP matches a threat intel indicator's NetworkIP, and the project adds ThreatType and Description explaining the match.
